source_text: Κοινωνεῖν γε μὴν ἄρτου καὶ τῶν ἀναγκαίων, ἃ πρὸς τὸν βίον ἀνθρώποις, δίκαιον. Εἰ γὰρ καὶ παραυτίκα τισὶ δόξεις ἀπολλύναι, ὥσπερ ὕδατι τὸν ἄρτον παραδιδοὺς, ἀλλ᾽ οὖν προϊόντος τοῦ χρόνου, οὐκ ἀνόνητός σοι φανεῖται ἡ φιλανθρωπία. Δίδου δὲ ἀφειδῶς, καὶ μέριζε τὰ σαυτοῦ πλείοσιν· οὐ γὰρ ἐπίστασαι τί ποτε ἡ ἐπιοῦσα ἐποίησεν ἡμέρα. Κατέχουσι δὲ οὐδὲ νεφέλαι τὸν ἑαυτῶν πολὺν ὑετὸν, ἀλλὰ τὸν ὄμβρον ἐπὶ γῆν ἀφιᾶσι· καὶ οὐδὲ δένδρον εἰς ἀεὶ ἕστηκεν, ἀλλὰ κἂν ἄνδρες αὐτοῦ φείσωνται, ἀνέμῳ γοῦν ἀνατραπήσεται. Πολλοὶ δὲ βούλονται καὶ τὰ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐσόμενα προγινώσκειν, καί τις εἴς τε νεφέλας ἀφορῶν, καὶ περιμένων ἄνεμον, ἀμήτου ἢ λικμητοῦ ἀπέσχετο, ἐπὶ μηδενὶ πεπεισμένος, μηδὲ γινώσκων τὶ τῶν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἐσομένων· ὥσπερ οὐδὲ οἷον ἡ κυοφοροῦσα τέξεται. Σπείρας δὲ ἐν καιρῷ, συγκόμιζε τοὺς καρποὺς, ὁπότ᾽ ἂν τούτου καιρὸς ἐνστῇ· ἄδηλον γὰρ, ὁποῖα αὐτῶν ἔσται ἀμείνω τῶν φυέντων. Γένοιτο δὲ ἅπαντα εἰς ἀγαθόν.
thought_title: Share bread and work without foreseeing the outcome
orientation: Solomon's teaching continues with commands about generosity and farming without knowing what will come from God.
pass_a_gloss: To share bread and the necessary things, which are for life for human beings, is just. For even if for the moment you will seem to some to be destroying it, as one handing over bread to water, yet as time advances, your love for mankind will not appear useless to you. Give unsparingly, and divide your own things to more people; for you do not know what the coming day has ever done. Clouds do not hold back their own abundant rain, but let go rain upon earth; and neither does a tree stand forever, but even if men spare it, at any rate by wind it will be overturned. Many want to know beforehand even the things to come from heaven, and someone both looking at clouds and waiting for wind held back from reaping or winnowing, persuaded by nothing, and knowing none of the things to come from God; just as neither what the pregnant woman will bear. Having sown in season, gather in the fruits, whenever the season of this comes; for it is unclear which of the grown things will be better. May all things turn out for good.

pass_b_english: It is right to share bread and the necessities of life with others. Even if for the moment some think you are throwing it away, like entrusting bread to the water (Ecclesiastes 11:1), your love for mankind will not prove useless to you as time goes on. So give unsparingly and share what is yours with many, for you do not know what the coming day will bring (Ecclesiastes 11:2).

The clouds do not hold back their own heavy rain but pour the shower down upon the earth, and no tree stands forever: even if people spare it, the wind will still bring it down (Ecclesiastes 11:3). Many want to know beforehand what will come from heaven, yet the man who watches the clouds and waits for the wind held back from reaping or winnowing (Ecclesiastes 11:4), with nothing to convince him and no knowledge of what will come from God, just as he does not know what the pregnant woman will bear (Ecclesiastes 11:5).

Once you have sown in season, gather in the fruits whenever the time for that comes, for it is unclear which of the things that grow will turn out better (Ecclesiastes 11:6). May all things turn out for good.
